title: Oculus: rolling spending limits for AI agent wallets
summary: Create a policy PDA for an agent, let the agent pass check_spend inside a window budget, then pause and close the policy.
what: Oculus Policy is an open Anchor program that enforces a rolling spending budget for an AI-agent wallet. An owner initialises a policy PDA seeded by ["policy", agent] with a daily limit (USDC micro-units) and a window between 60 and 86400 seconds. The agent must sign check_spend, which rolls the window if it has expired, rejects over-budget attempts, and otherwise increments spent_window. The owner can pause or close the policy. Upstream is the program only; the hosted app is Sol.College's generic IDL console pointed at this devnet deployment.
app_note: The fork has no first-party frontend. The page at /dapps/oculus/ is the generic IDL-driven wallet console, with this devnet program id filled in.

diagram:
owner ─ init_policy(agent, limit, window) ─▶ Policy PDA ["policy", agent]
agent ─ check_spend(amount, memo) ─▶ roll window if expired; reject if paused or over limit; else spent_window += amount
owner ─ pause_agent(reason) ─▶ paused=true
owner ─ close_policy() ─▶ account closed to owner
accounts: Owner, agent, daily_limit_usdc, window_seconds, spent_window, paused, bump.
The human or treasury that issues and can pause or close the policy.
Signer on check_spend; pubkey is a seed of the PDA
The AI-agent wallet whose spends must pass the budget check.

instructions.name: init_policy
steps: Rejects zero or too-high limits and window_seconds outside 60..=86400.
Initialises the policy PDA, paid by the owner.

instructions.name: check_spend
steps: Agent must match policy.agent and the policy must not be paused.
Rolls the window if expired, then rejects LimitExceeded or increments spent_window. Does not transfer tokens.

instructions.name: pause_agent
steps: Owner-only. Sets paused=true and stores a u8 reason.

instructions.name: close_policy
steps: Owner-only. Closes the PDA and returns rent to the owner.

innovation.title: A reusable on-chain budget check for agent wallets, not a token transfer
innovation.text: check_spend is deliberately a gate, not a payment: another program or off-chain flow can require a successful check before settlement. The interesting DeAI idea is an inspectable rolling budget the runtime itself enforces, plus pause and close for the owner.
innovation.more: The window-reset path was not waited out in this run.

frontend.title: Generic IDL console
steps: init_policy derives the policy PDA from ["policy", agent].
check_spend must be signed by that agent key.

exercises.title: Why does an over-limit check emit LimitBreached but not change spent_window?
steps: Read the LimitExceeded branch in check_spend.
exercises.expect: It emits and returns err before assigning spent_window = next.
exercises.hint: check_spend.rs around the next > daily_limit_usdc test.

exercises.title: What windows are legal?
steps: Find the require! on window_seconds in init_policy.

not_covered: The window-reset path was not waited out (would need window_seconds to elapse). check_spend does not transfer tokens. The hosted UI was not clicked in headless Chromium in this run.
objectives: Create a policy PDA seeded by an agent pubkey and read it back.
Explain the check_spend budget and pause checks.
Pause and close a policy as the owner.
prereqs: A wallet on devnet with a little SOL (init_policy pays rent).
Comfort with PDAs and Anchor account constraints.
